concepts.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Refine this two-view house concept plate, retaining its same house identity, warm painted outline style, palette, doors, domestic details, roof shapes, chimney placement, camera elevation and true opposite front-right / rear-left viewpoints. Keep both entire buildings and every roof, chimney and foundation inside the sheet with generous ivory margins; slightly reduce the overall plate scale to make room if necessary. No labels or text. The current tall lodging house has only THREE full floors. Add EXACTLY ONE additional complete upper residential floor to BOTH views, with a consistent pair of windows and structural floor band, so it has FOUR FULL STOREYS (ground floor + THREE upper floors) plus the same small attic under the steep clay gable. Keep the narrow footprint, modest domestic style and attached low rear pantry. The result must be visibly tall and slender, not simply the same three-floor house with a taller roof.
concepts.name: Lantern Row lodging house
concepts.storeys: Four storeys plus a small attic
concepts.role: Narrow upper-town gaps and distant vertical accents
concepts.design: A TALL NARROW lodging house, FOUR full storeys plus a small attic under a steep front-facing terracotta gable. Approximately 4.5 m street frontage by 7 m deep. Clearly taller than it is wide: only two modest domestic windows across each upper frontage, one recessed dark-teal entry at ground level, limestone ground storey and faded warm cream/ochre plaster above. Simple oak floor bands, a shallow supported timber jetty at the second level, one small attic window in the gable and one slim brick chimney beside the rear-right roof edge. The right wall is relatively plain warm plaster, suitable for a neighbour standing close. Rear has two narrow window stacks, a modest ground service door and a low narrow tiled pantry projection at the foot of one side. A short washing line stays under the back eaves. Quiet residential character, clearly four full levels, no tower or public-building features. Roof and small chimney should give a useful thin skyline silhouette.

concepts.name: Saltwind apartment house
concepts.role: Continuous residential blocks behind the square
concepts.design: A BROAD MEDIUM-HEIGHT THREE-STOREY apartment house, approximately 10 m wide by 7 m deep. Rectangular mass with a LOW HIPPED deep-teal tiled roof and two squat brick chimney stacks, no attic storey or tower. Pale buttery plaster over a limestone ground floor, warm honey-oak window lintels and faded blue-green shutters; three regularly spaced window bays across the street facade, a single recessed central entry with a small practical stone hood. Use a few simple window boxes and pale linen curtains, not a mass of ivy. Continuous clear horizontal eaves make it read wider and calmer than a narrow gabled house. The rear has the same three levels with a quieter window rhythm, a ground utility door, a small covered shared laundry alcove and rain barrel. One end wall is almost plain, suitable for a close neighbour. Entire roof, rear wall and both end facades visible across the paired views.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: detailed architectural concept plate for BACKGROUND RESIDENTIAL HOUSES in the same seaside town as the references. Create one specific residential asset shown from TWO COMPLEMENTARY OPPOSITE orthographic corners, side by side. These buildings fill the streets and roofscape beyond the playable area, so their roof mass, floor count and readable domestic windows matter.
Reference image 1: approved Guildhall Square, for town palette, density and architectural family only. Reference images 2 and 3: previous seaside building plates, for painted outlines, stone/plaster/timber craft and two-view presentation only. Use the new residential design below, rather than their public/trade buildings.
LAYOUT AND CAMERA: landscape 1536x1024 or larger, warm ivory paper background. LEFT PANEL is FRONT plus RIGHT wall, looking from southeast. RIGHT PANEL is the BACK plus LEFT wall of the SAME building, exactly 180 degrees around. This must reveal all FOUR facades between the pair, not repeat the same side wall from two corners. Fixed orthographic parallel projection, about 31 degrees downward elevation and 45-degree diagonal azimuth to the walls, matching the game. Vertical lines parallel, no perspective convergence or fisheye. Both views have exactly the same scale, footprint, storey heights, roof shape, dormers, chimney positions and attached rear volume, physically rotated rather than mirrored or redesigned. The front door must be on the opposite hidden facade in the rear view. A one-sided extension should move to its geometrically correct side when rotated.
FRAMING: show complete roof ridges, chimneys, eaves, every floor down to foundations and any small rear lean-to. At least 6 percent blank margin and a clean gap between views. Thin paving/foundation under the asset only; no cliff, sea diorama, full street or giant surrounding garden. Nothing cropped. No people, robots, labels, lettering, signs, dimensions, watermark or comparison scale figures.
VISUAL STYLE: high-detail warm painted concept art with proper dark-brown outer outlines and clean joinery lines, like the references. Readable large roof and wall forms, fine painted clay tiles, pale dressed limestone, softly salt-worn plaster, honey oak details, muted teal/sage/coral shutters, iron hinges and practical gutters. Believable doors and windows at consistent human scale. Habitation through a few open/closed shutters, simple curtains, patched roof tiles, chimney pots, a small rain barrel, a little rear washing or modest plants. Keep clutter and ornamental brass restrained. Clear silhouettes and calm domestic facades should remain useful when viewed far away.
RESIDENTIAL FUNCTION: ordinary lived-in homes that belong between town buildings. No storefront display glazing, trade emblems, civic clocks, cupolas, elaborate towers, heroic mechanical centrepieces or huge balconies. This is a distinct house size/roof type within a coherent town family.
SPECIFIC DESIGN:
A BROAD MEDIUM-HEIGHT THREE-STOREY apartment house, approximately 10 m wide by 7 m deep. Rectangular mass with a LOW HIPPED deep-teal tiled roof and two squat brick chimney stacks, no attic storey or tower. Pale buttery plaster over a limestone ground floor, warm honey-oak window lintels and faded blue-green shutters; three regularly spaced window bays across the street facade, a single recessed central entry with a small practical stone hood. Use a few simple window boxes and pale linen curtains, not a mass of ivy. Continuous clear horizontal eaves make it read wider and calmer than a narrow gabled house. The rear has the same three levels with a quieter window rhythm, a ground utility door, a small covered shared laundry alcove and rain barrel. One end wall is almost plain, suitable for a close neighbour. Entire roof, rear wall and both end facades visible across the paired views.

concepts.name: Rosewash lane house
concepts.storeys: Two storeys plus a roof loft
concepts.role: Ordinary side streets and gaps between taller neighbours
concepts.design: A COMPACT TWO-STOREY lane home with a small roof loft, approximately 5.5 m frontage by 6 m deep. Warm pale SALMON/ROSE limewashed upper walls over a pale stone ground floor, oak corner posts and a modest supported upper-floor jetty. A simple asymmetrical gabled CLAY-TILE roof with one off-centre little shed dormer and a brick chimney at its left-rear edge. A sage-green front door at one side of the ground facade, one domestic ground window and two upper windows with partly open shutters. The side has just one narrow stair window, not another shopfront. Rear includes a shallow one-storey pantry lean-to with a sloping tiled roof, a practical kitchen door, stacked firewood and a few pots close to the wall. This is a believable small inhabited family house, with distinct rose plaster and a simple slightly uneven roof silhouette, no dramatic balcony or turret.

concepts.name: Shingle Court cottage
concepts.role: Low courtyards, roof gaps and the lower edges of views
concepts.design: A LOW WIDE courtyard cottage, just ONE FULL STOREY plus a modest roof loft, approximately 8.5 m wide by 5.5 m deep. Broad pale limestone and chalk-plaster walls, a long warm terracotta pitched roof with two small low dormers, and one short chimney stack at an end. concepts.name: Eaveside terrace pair
concepts.role: Dense residential rows and varied roofs beyond the playable boundary

No whole street or extra third/fourth house; just this one useful joined two-home background cluster.
